Definition: probably from an obsolete ὄρω (to rise or "rear"; perhaps akin to G142; compare G3733); a mountain (as lifting itself above the plain):--hill, mount(-ain).
BiblicalUsage: The mountain is the high place of the Bible. Paul says faith that could remove mountains is nothing without charity, Peter remembers being with Jesus on the holy mount, the disciples returned from the mount called Olivet after the ascension, and Sinai stands as the mountain of the old covenant.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced the mountain is where God meets His people: Sinai, Olivet, the mount of transfiguration — and the faith that can move a mountain is the faith that trusts Him on the plain. And when the mountain will not move, I remember that the God of the mountain is with me on the plain.
